slides.heading: Spiral Traverse
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Spiral Traverse, a medium arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Read a (possibly non-square) matrix in clockwise spiral order.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Read a (possibly non-square) matrix in clockwise spiral order.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Peel the matrix layer by layer: top row, right column, bottom row, left column, then shrink.
slides.narration: Peel the matrix layer by layer: top row, right column, bottom row, left column, then shrink.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Simulation with a visited matrix and direction turns → O(n) time, O(n) space
Layer by layer with four boundaries → O(n), O(1) extra
slides.narration: One approach walks with a direction and turns when it hits a visited cell, which needs a visited matrix. Shrinking four boundaries layer by layer avoids that extra memory.

slides.heading: Approach
slides.narration: Step by step. First, keep four boundaries. Second, walk the perimeter. Third, guard single rows or columns. Fourth, shrink and repeat.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Layer 0: right col, bottom row, left col
slides.narration: Layer 0, right col, bottom row, left col: we add 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Layer 1: right col, bottom row, left col
slides.narration: Layer 1, right col, bottom row, left col: we add 15, 16.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We keep start and end row and column. Each loop walks the top row, the right column, then the bottom row and left column with guards for single rows or columns, and finally shrinks all four boundaries.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n cells. Space is O of n output.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Single row or single column — don't double count
slides.narration: The trickiest cases are a single remaining row or column, where the bottom and left passes would repeat cells. The guards sr less than er and sc less than ec prevent that.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: A natural follow-up is the reverse: filling an n by n matrix with one to n squared in spiral order.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Peel the matrix layer by layer: top row, right column, bottom row, left column, then shrink.
slides.narration: To recap Spiral Traverse: Peel the matrix layer by layer: top row, right column, bottom row, left column, then shrink. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
